notes:
Round 2. The requirement changed (exact-phrase queries), so three contracts were deprecated and
superseded rather than edited: inverted-index -> positional-index (frequencies cannot express
adjacency), search-cli -> search-cli-phrases (quoting is new surface), ranked-search ->
ranked-phrase-search (the deliverable itself). corpus-reader and text-analyzer were untouched — the
tokenizer is exactly what a phrase is tokenized with — and bm25-ranking kept its statement and was
only re-pointed at the new index contract, which is the protocol's reverse cascade repair.

phrase-matching is the one genuinely new child: it owns adjacency, nothing else. Keeping it out of
bm25-ranking is what let relevance stay bit-identical (0.2560 / 0.8533) across a format change.

Every successor gate runs its predecessor's gate as well as its own. That is the regression rule made
structural: "nothing that worked may break" is not a promise in a note, it is the deprecated
contract's own assertions still running inside the successor's acceptance command.

Dimensions after the change (node bench/measure.mjs):
  relevance   meanP10 0.2560, meanRecall10 0.8533   unchanged to four decimals
  phrase      precision 1.0, recall 1.0 over 539 labelled queries (333 of them deliberately empty)
  size        0.3727 (was 0.3148) — the one dimension positions cost; laws/index-size.json raised
              0.32 -> 0.38 deliberately, with the encoding work done first (naive: 0.4725)
  speed       p95 ~90 ms, half of the sample now phrase queries (the position-decoding path)
  robustness  120 / 5 / exit 0, unchanged
The phrase ground truth in bench/queries.json is a brute-force adjacency scan that knows nothing
about the index, and a third of the labelled sets are empty on purpose: a filter that never filters
scores perfectly on matching phrases alone.
